purpose: A single-line text field with its label, hint and error wired together. OtpInput is the same field split into one box per character for a one-time code.
$operationsNote: Mirrors shared/core/agent/field.ts, which is what the runtime dispatches on. source/components/shared/core/agent/__tests__/field-passport.test.ts fails if the two drift. No `apiMethod`: a field is written through its ref — the element for most of these, a handle for Combobox and DatePicker — and that is a normal case, not a gap.

setValue.summary: Write a value into the field, as though a person had entered it.

focus.summary: Move keyboard focus to the field.

supplied: the label is a real <label> bound to the input, so clicking it focuses the field
description and error are linked by aria-describedby
the character counter is a live region when `showCount` is on
OtpInput moves focus between boxes and handles paste of a whole code
required: a `label`, or `aria-label` when the field is visually unlabelled
`type` matching the data — email, tel, url — so the right keyboard and autofill appear
`autoComplete` on anything a browser or password manager should fill

composition.notes: The component renders its own <label> and <input>. Wrapping it in another label binds the text to the wrong control and breaks the click target.

safeMutations.rationale: Appearance and affordances are safe. `value` and `name` are the form's data, `type`/`pattern`/`mask` decide what is accepted, and `error` is the host's verdict on validity — an agent that writes it is claiming a validation result it did not compute.

propNotes.mask: Shapes what can be typed. Changing it can make an already-valid value unreachable.
propNotes.length: OtpInput only: the number of boxes, which is also the expected code length.
propNotes.error: Set by the host after validating. The component never derives it.
